title: The City Inequality Question: What Metropolitan Data Reveals
summary: City-level inequality reveals local differences that national averages conceal, while a coverage audit shows how little of the urban world is measured consistently.
key_takeaway: National averages need a metropolitan lens, and the metropolitan lens needs a serious coverage audit before it can support credible comparison.

inline_figures.caption: City-level monitoring depth is uneven, with a limited group observed repeatedly and many represented only a few times.
The lowest and highest latest available city observations reveal a wide inequality range across the 2010–2017 source window.
Data-rich countries occupy different inequality bands and show different amounts of variation across observed city-years.
Median Gini trajectories for the best-covered countries are shown with the range across their observed cities.
